clue.text: Old king's comfort, being fat!

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a past British monarch
comfort means ease

explanation.surface: A bygone monarch takes his ease and grows plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is animal fat or oily matter, so the noun fat is a synonym.

clue.text: Wot's up? Rossers catch the old floater in Suffolk

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: wot's is a jokey spelling of what's, written as wots

indicators.note: the police catch, or hold, the boat between their letters

parts.note: rozzers (spelt here with s) is British slang for the police, i.e. the Met, London's Metropolitan Police
Noah's Ark is the famous floating vessel of old

explanation.surface: A slangy cry of alarm as police haul in an ancient boat somewhere in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rossers' is the setter's spelling of rozzers, British slang for police, here the Met. STOWMARKET is a market town in Suffolk, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowmarket is a town located in the county of Suffolk, so 'in Suffolk' points to a place there.

clue.text: Nearly all power unknown is invincible

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: power means might
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Something nearly all-powerful and mysterious cannot be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almighty is God, all-powerful, so as an adjective it means having unlimited power, unbeatable.

clue.text: The one who pulls back gets the thanks

indicators.note: pulling back suggests the word for the puller is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, i.e. pulls

explanation.surface: The person who hauls something back is rewarded with gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a recompense given as thanks for a service.

clue.text: Rebound of echo: trick endlessly played

indicators.note: played means the letters are arranged in a new way, like notes played
endlessly means the last letter of the word is lost

explanation.surface: A bounced sound is an echo trick played without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TRICK to TRIC; 'played' then rearranges ECHO plus TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a rebound of a projectile off a surface.

clue.text: Bridge? It's easy!

definitions.meaning: a bridge is something you go across on foot, i.e. a structure to cross
an easy win or task with no real contest

explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is an easy victory, and jokingly a bridge is something one walks over.

clue.text: Gossip on board? They'll follow relentlessly

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside the steamship's letters

parts.note: on board conventionally means within SS, a steamship
a gossip is a talker

explanation.surface: Chatter on a ship about people who pursue others obsessively.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalkers are people who pursue someone persistently, so they follow relentlessly.

clue.text: Follow precedent in the City house

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Doing what has always been done in a City of London building.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to imitate or repeat what was done before.

clue.text: Say nothing to curdle the sauce

indicators.note: to curdle is to change and spoil, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A cook keeps quiet as the sauce goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya sauce is a common condiment, so soya names the sauce.

clue.text: Neckwear retrieved from a central location

indicators.note: retrieved suggests coming back, so the run is read backwards
from shows the letters are taken out of the words

explanation.surface: Something to wear round the neck recovered from a central spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar is a band of material worn around the neck.

clue.text: Wisdom thus exemplified: how silly

annotationWithheld.why: Wisdom thus exemplified: how silly (8). The anagram of HOW SILLY needs 'silly' both as fodder and as the anagram indicator; no other word signals the anagram.

clue.text: Mishap to go round after work: devise steps to be taken

annotationWithheld.why: Mishap to go round after work: devise steps to be taken (11). CHORE (work) leaves OGRAPH, which no reading of 'Mishap to go round' gives; no source found to explain it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mishap to go round after work: devise steps to be taken

clue.text: Ugly woman writer served with biscuits?

parts.note: a gorgon is a hideous woman, from the Gorgons of myth
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A hideous woman author is handed biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue cheese, typically eaten with crackers or biscuits.

clue.text: Man of the theatre once with introductions to young lady turning up in yellow

parts.note: Noel Coward was a celebrated 20th-century playwright and actor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top
introductions are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An old stage figure introduced to a young woman in a yellow outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introductions to' takes Y and L, and 'turning up' reverses them to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for lacking courage, which is a synonym of cowardly.

clue.text: Celebrated part of speech heard during run up-river

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: during means one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, up means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a British river

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken, giving a spelling with the same sound

parts.note: a noun is a part of speech

explanation.surface: A grammatical term spoken while running upstream earns fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Britain; 'up' turns it round to sit after R, and the sound-alike spelling of the grammatical term goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means famous, the same as celebrated.

clue.text: Chucker-out to dismiss soldiers

parts.note: to eject is to throw out, dismiss
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A bouncer is told to throw out the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector is something or someone that throws things out, a chucker-out.

clue.text: Run through team of loud Poles painting all over

indicators.note: all over means everything is turned over, the whole run read backwards

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team
F stands for forte, loud in music
S and N are the south and north poles
painting is art

explanation.surface: A squad of noisy Poles splashes paint everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is to pierce through, as with a spear, so to run through.

clue.text: Aperture for skeleton?

parts.note: a skeleton key is a key that opens many locks, so its aperture is the slot it goes in

explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a type of key, and the opening it fits is the hole in a lock.

clue.text: Sherry party? After all, I am not whacked

indicators.note: after places the party at the end
whacked means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: At a sherry party someone protests that, after all, they are not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of medium-dry sherry from Spain.

clue.text: Shed a little off the perpendicular?

definitions.meaning: a shed whose roof slopes against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall, and leaning to means tilting off vertical.

clue.text: Copied for beginners to add page each day

indicators.note: beginners are the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Instructions for novices to add a page every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Aped means imitated, which is copying.

clue.text: Make love at sun-up? It's serious

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Romance at dawn turns out to be a weighty matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, a grave and serious thing.

clue.text: Little draughts — that's about the end!

parts.note: draughts of beer are often served as pints

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is
Z is the last letter of the alphabet, the end

explanation.surface: Small sips of drink provoke an exasperated cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pint-size means very small, little.

clue.text: Forgiveness is even academic

parts.note: par means equal or even
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Being forgiven is just as scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardon is an act of forgiving an offence.

clue.text: Learner with record pile slipped

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: slipped means the pile has fallen into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student whose pile of records has toppled over.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower who learns from a teacher.

clue.text: Remained sober, I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told signals something heard, a word spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on without drinking, by report.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means remained in place.
